title: Geo-tiered data controls & self-serve contract wizard: subprocessor scoping + flexible retention SKUs
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Scope: Build a self-serve contract wizard and pricing experiment that lets enterprise prospects configure (1) geographic data residency commitments, (2) retention windows as selectable SKUs, and (3) an explicit subprocessor exposure summary + attestation generator used in sales SLO and security questionnaires. Goals: reduce time-to-contract for mid-market & enterprise deals, capture elasticity in pricing for retention tiers, and provide a single artifact (contract wizard PDF + attestation CSV) that maps legal commitments to billing SKU. Out-of-scope: custom negotiated language for >$500k ARR deals (handled by AE/legal).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Wizard renders 3 residency regions (US, EU/UK, APAC) and outputs a contract appendix with SCC selection logic; 2) Customer can select from three retention SKUs (7d, 90d, 1y) and the system computes delta price estimate; 3) Generated attestation lists active subprocessors by functional bucket and includes timestamps and vendor-country matrix; 4) Sales can email a PDF + CSV bundle from the wizard and track in Deal metadata; 5) Legal confirms template maps to standard DPA clauses and passes initial Securty review.
success_metrics: - % reduction in time from first contact to signed DPA for self-serve eligible customers; - Conversion lift for mid-market trials >10% when retention SKU pricing is shown; - # of deals using wizard vs manual redlines; - Ticket volume to Legal for standard requests falls by 45%.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overpromising residence guarantees for third-party subprocessors. Mitigation: add explicit disclaimer and 'operationally available' phrasing; keep SCC auto-selection conservative and include fallback language. Risk: Pricing complexity confuses buyers. Mitigation: show clear delta pricing and monthly equivalents; run A/B experiment with simplified vs granular SKU.
open_questions: - Should SCC auto-selection prefer EU-to-EU subprocessors only, or allow EU->US with standard SCCs+addendum?; - What minimum contract term must be required for 1y retention SKU?; - How to represent hybrid storage (cache KVs ephemeral but backups retained)?
implementation_notes: Frontend: new wizard flow under Console > Contracts; backend: pricing service endpoint to compute delta, CSV attestation generator, template rendering service. Engineering tasks tracked in ENG-7842 (wizard API) and ENG-7901 (attestation generator). Design prototypes in DES-1103. Use Confluence doc for clause mapping and canonical text.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff meeting with Legal, Sales, and Engineering. Agreed to MVP: 3 regions + 3 retention SKUs. Legal provided initial DPA appendix draft.
2026-02-18: PM reviewed price sensitivity matrix with Growth. Proposed per-GB-month deltas for retention tiers; Growth suggested showing monthly equivalent and annual commitment option.

2026-02-24: Design (DES-1103) delivered low-fi flows. UX feedback: reduce cognitive load by collapsing subprocessor details behind an expand CTA; Sales requested exportable CSV for security questionnaires.
2026-02-28: Eng scoping session; estimated 5 points. Dependency: pricing service needs a small extension to calculate retention premium (ENG-7842).

2026-03-03: Legal review comments received: 1) tighten wording around 'data residency' to reflect that backups may cross borders for DR; 2) require SCC addendum when customer selects EU-only residency. Action: update template and surface SCC checkbox in wizard.
2026-03-05: Prototype demo to Sales Ops. Sales Ops requested a toggle 'Allow standard subprocessors' to mark customers who require zero-third-party-exposure. Added to backlog as follow-up (PM-64902).
